title: Prefix systemd timers/services for healthchecks
body:
### Feature request description

When containers define healthchecks, Podman uses systemd timers/services to execute them. These systemd units are named with some (random?) hashes, like `945e8d1001930adc728d58b154bafcf3ce2c26f406cb97d6c834358b1f856f72-49985e258867c94d.service`. Because these hashes are quite long, they can clutter the logs. As hashes can use any initial letter, they are apread all over the place in the list of system services, and aren't grouped nicely together. Also, they don't contain any indication that they come from Podman, so without extra research, you can't know where they come from and what they are used for.

### Suggest potential solution

All these systemd units should have a common prefix, like `podman-healthchecks-`, so, for example `podman-healthchecks-945e8d1001930adc728d58b154bafcf3ce2c26f406cb97d6c834358b1f856f72-49985e258867c94d.service`. This way, it is immediately clear that they come from Podman healthchecks, all of them are grouped nicely in the (alphabetic) list of all units, and it is easier to exclude them from various log collection services.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Potentially, this prefix could also be configurable. In any case, I think the default value should be something like `podman-healthchecks-`.
